workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§198–199
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§198–199: The Merkid scattered, and Sübegetei sent after them
part: §§198–199 — The Merkid scattered, and Sübegetei sent after them
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§198–199, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: §198 closes the campaign against the Merkid and Küchülüg of the Naiman: Toqto'a falls to a stray arrow, his sons flee west, and the Merkid left behind are broken up. §199 gives Chinggis’s charge to Sübegetei, sent after the fugitives, and the rules he lays down for the march: how to spare the horses and the food, and how the hunt on the road is to be kept in bounds.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Merkid irgen daγ̇uližu

morph.gloss: the Merkid, a people (the -d is probably a plural) [種名]
to plunder, take captive (stem inferred from the Ming 擄) [擄着]

sentences.l: Merkid people plundering,
sentences.i: Having plundered the Merkid people,
sentences.n: This part opens in the middle of the campaign against the Merkid, with a converb in -žu: daγ̇uližu is daγ̇uli- “plunder, take captive” (Ming 擄; the stem is inferred) and -žu “-ing”. No subject is named in these first words; Chinggis is understood, as the units below show. Merkid ends in -d, probably a plural, as in other parts.

sentences.t: Toγtoγ̇a-Beki-jin jeke köġün Qudu-jin Qatud Tügei, Döregene žirin-eče Döregene-ji tende Ögödei Qaγan-(n)a ögbe.

morph.gloss: Toqto'a Beki, a man's name [人名 的]
genitive: of (after a vowel) [人名 的]
the two, a pair (read from the Ming 兩箇; the stem is uncertain) [兩箇內]
ablative: from, out of (front-vowel form; Ming 內 'among') [兩箇內]
Döregene, a woman's name [(婦人)名 行]
accusative: object marker (the Ming 行) [(婦人)名 行]
there, then (locative adverb from tere 'that') [那裏]
qan, sovereign, emperor (the title, given to Ögödei by hindsight) [皇帝 行]
dative-locative: to (back-vowel form; the Ming marks it 行) [皇帝 行]

sentences.l: Toγtoγ̇a-Beki’s great son Qudu’s ladies Tügei, Döregene, from the two Döregene-(object) there to Ögödei Qaγan gave.
sentences.i: Of the wives of Qudu, the eldest son of Toqto'a Beki, Tügei and Döregene, he gave Döregene to Ögödei Qahan.
sentences.n: Read the genitives from the front: Toγtoγ̇a-Beki-jin … köġün Qudu-jin Qatud, “Toqto'a Beki’s great son Qudu’s ladies”; -jin is the genitive after a vowel (Ming 的). jeke köġün is “great son”; “eldest” is my reading of the Ming 大, not proved. Qatud is qatun with the plural -d (Ming 娘子每). žirin-eče is “from among the two” (Ming 兩箇內; the stem žirin is read from the Ming alone). Döregene-ji is the accusative; Qaγan-(n)a is the dative-locative, which the Ming writes 行 (“to”), and the title is given to Ögödei by hindsight. The giver is not named; Chinggis is understood. ögbe is ög- “give” in the past.

sentences.t: Merkid-ün žarimud ulus daižižu taiqal qorγa qorγalažuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: the Merkid, a people [種名 的]
genitive: of (after a consonant) [種名 的]
to turn hostile (from dain 'enemy'; Ming 反) [反着]
hilltop, summit (read from the Ming 山頂) [山頂]

words.reading: 中豁舌兒中合剌主爲 qorγalažuγ̇ui

morph.gloss: to fortify (from qorγa; Ming 寨子把) [寨子把了]

sentences.l: Merkid’s half people turning hostile, hilltop fort fortified.
sentences.i: Half of the Merkid people turned hostile and fortified a stronghold on a hilltop.
sentences.n: A new subject: Merkid-ün žarimud ulus, “the half of the Merkid people” (žarim “half, some” with the plural -ud; Ming 一半). daižižu is daiži- “turn hostile” (from dain “enemy”) with the converb -žu. qorγa qorγalažuγ̇ui plays on one stem: qorγa “fort” (Ming 寨子), qorγala- “to fortify” (寨子把), so “fort fortified”; -žuγ̇ui is the narrative past. taiqal “hilltop” is read from the Ming 山頂 alone.

sentences.t: Tende Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:

morph.gloss: there, then (locative adverb from tere 'that') [那裏]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: There Čiṅgis Qaγan decree when making:
sentences.i: Then Chinggis Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: žarliγ bolurun, literally “decree, when becoming (making)”, is the formula that introduces a decree: bol- with the time-converb -urun (Ming 做的). It recurs three times in this part. tende “there” (Ming 那裏) is here “then, at that point”.

sentences.t: "Sorγan-Šira-jin köġün Čimbai-ji nojalažu žeġün γar-un čeriġüd(i)-jer qorγalaγsad Merkid-i eġereġülün ilebe.

morph.gloss: Sorqan-Shira, a man's name [人名 的]
genitive: of (after a vowel) [人名 的]
Chimbai, a man's name [人名 行]
accusative: object marker (the Ming 行) [人名 行]
to make or act as commander (from noyan 'lord'; stem inferred from the Ming 官做) [官做着]
genitive: of (after a consonant, back-vowel form) [手的]

words.reading: 扯舌里兀的-耶舌兒 čeriġüd(i)-jer

morph.gloss: soldier, army (compare čeri in čeriġüd-te) [軍(每)領着]
plural (the vowel is Shiratori’s linking -ü-; the glossary reads čeriġüdi as čerig + -üd) [軍(每)領着]
instrumental: with (the (i) is Shiratori’s) [軍(每)領着]

words.reading: 中豁舌兒中合剌黑撒惕 qorγalaγsad

glyphs.s: 中豁舌兒中合剌黑撒惕

morph.gloss: past participle plural: those who had … [寨子把了的每]
accusative: object marker (the Ming 行) [種名行]
to attack (stem inferred from the Ming 攻) [敎攻]

sentences.l: Sorγan-Šira’s son Čimbai-(object) commander-making, left hand’s troops-with, fortified Merkid-(object) attack-causing sent.
sentences.i: He made Chimbai, son of Sorqan-Shira, a commander and sent him with the troops of the left hand to attack the Merkid who had fortified themselves.
sentences.n: Shiratori opens a quotation mark before Sorγan-Šira-jin and never closes it. Because ilebe is a narrative past (“sent”), not a command, I give the decree as reported narrative, without marks. Čimbai-ji nojalažu is the accusative with nojala- “make (or act as) a commander” (Ming 官做着; stem inferred from noyan). žeġün γar-un is “of the left hand” (Ming 左 手的), the left wing; čeriġüd(i)-jer is the instrumental “with” on the plural of čerig, the (i) being Shiratori’s. qorγalaγsad is the plural past participle “those who had fortified”, and Merkid-i stands beside it: “the fortified ones, the Merkid”. eġereġülün is a causative converb; eġere- “attack” rests on the Ming 攻 alone.

sentences.t: Toγtoγ̇a, Qudu, Čilaγ̇un köġud(i)-jer(i)-jen čüġen bejes daižižu γaruγsan-i

morph.gloss: instrumental: with (the (i) is Shiratori's) [子每 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form) [子每 自的行]
bare, with only one's body, stripped (perhaps beje 'body' + -s; uncertain) [罄身(每)]
to go out [出了的 行]
past participle: who has …-ed [出了的 行]
accusative: object marker (the Ming 行) [出了的 行]

sentences.l: Toγtoγ̇a, Qudu, Čilaγ̇un, with their own sons, few, bare-bodied, turning hostile, the ones who went out-(object)
sentences.i: As for Toqto'a, Qudu and Chila'un, who had turned hostile and gone out with their own sons, a few men with nothing but themselves,
sentences.n: This unit is an object waiting for its verb, which comes in the next unit (nekežü). γaruγsan-i is γar- “go out” + the past participle -γsan + the accusative -i (Ming 行): “the one(s) who went out”. köġud(i)-jer(i)-jen, “with their own sons”, stacks köġü “son”, the plural -d, the instrumental -jer and the reflexive -jen, with two (i)s that are Shiratori’s. čüġen bejes is “few, bare-bodied”: the Ming 罄身 means stripped, with only the body; bejes may be beje “body” plus -s, but that is uncertain.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan nekežü

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to pursue, chase (stem inferred from the Ming 追襲) [追襲着]

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan pursuing,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan, pursuing them,
sentences.n: nekežü is neke- “pursue” (stem inferred from the Ming 追襲, which can also mean “attack”) with the converb -žü; it takes up the accusative γaruγsan-i of the unit above. A converb chain runs through the next few units, broken here at its natural joints.

sentences.t: Altai-jin ebür-e übülžežü

morph.gloss: front, the front side (Ming 前) [前(行)]
makes a verb: to winter [住冬着]

sentences.l: Altai’s front-to wintering,
sentences.i: wintered at the front of the Altai,
sentences.n: ebür-e is ebür “front” (Ming 前) with the dative-locative -e; elsewhere in these parts ebür is the “front” or “bosom” of a mountain or cliff, and I leave it as “front” rather than guess a compass side. übülžežü is übül “winter” made a verb with -že- (“to winter”; the Ming 住冬着, “staying the winter”, supports it) and the converb -žü. Altai-jin is the genitive after a vowel (Ming 山名的).

sentences.t: hüker žil qabur Arai-ijar dabažu oduγ̇asu

morph.gloss: Arai, a mountain (Ming 山名) [山名(依着)]
instrumental: by way of, along (the Ming 依着) [山名(依着)]
to cross over a pass [越着]
to go (stem inferred from the Ming 去) [去呵]
conditional: if, when (the u is a linking vowel) [去呵]

sentences.l: Ox year spring Arai by-way-of crossing, if going,
sentences.i: In the spring of the Ox year, when he went on, crossing by way of Mount Arai,
sentences.n: hüker žil is the Ox year of the twelve-animal cycle, qabur “spring”. Arai-ijar is the instrumental -ijar, “by way of, along” (Ming 依着), on a mountain name (Ming 山名). oduγ̇asu is od- “go” with -uγ̇asu “if, when” (Ming 呵); the Ming particle 呵 marks a clause that sets the time for the next. The one who goes is Chinggis; the main verb is in the unit ending ažuγ̇ui.

sentences.t: Naiman-u Küčülüg Qān ulus(i)-jan abqaγ̇ulžu

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (short form beside qaγan) [(皇帝)]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (back-vowel form; the (i) is Shiratori's) [百姓 自的行]

sentences.l: Naiman’s Küčülüg Qān, his own people having had taken,
sentences.i: Küchülüg Qan of the Naiman, having gathered his people,
sentences.n: abqaγ̇ulžu is ab- “take” with a causative -qaγ̇ul- (shape uncertain) and the converb -žu; the Ming 敎要着 means “having caused to be taken”. Because the reflexive -(i)jan points back to Küchülüg, I read “had his own people taken up” as “gathered his people about him”. Qān here is the short form of the title, as in §§196–197.

sentences.t: tere daižižu γaruγsaγ̇ar

morph.gloss: that, that one (demonstrative and third-person pronoun) [那]

words.reading: 中合舌魯黑撒阿舌兒 γaruγsaγ̇ar

morph.gloss: past participle -γsan + instrumental -γ̇ar: since having …-ed (Ming 以來) [出了以來]

sentences.l: that turning hostile, since going out,
sentences.i: since he had rebelled and gone out,
sentences.n: tere “that one” (Ming 那) is, I read, Küchülüg, who had turned hostile and left; the Ming does not say so, and the reading is mine. γaruγsaγ̇ar is γar- “go out” + the participle -γsan + the instrumental -γ̇ar; the Ming 以來 “ever since” is the only evidence for “since having gone out”.

sentences.t: čüġen küġün Merkid-ün Toγtoγ̇a qojar neiležü

morph.gloss: the Merkid, a people [種名 的]
genitive: of (after a consonant) [種名 的]
two (it follows the pair it counts) [兩箇]
to join, come together (Ming 相合) [相合着]

sentences.l: few men, Merkid’s Toγtoγ̇a, the two joining,
sentences.i: he and Toqto'a of the Merkid, the two of them with few men, joined together,
sentences.n: qojar “two” follows the pair it counts: Toγtoγ̇a qojar, “Toqto'a, the two”; the pair is Küchülüg and Toqto'a, though only Toqto'a is named, Küchülüg being carried over from above. neiležü is neile- “join” (Ming 相合) + -žü. čüġen küġün is “few men” (Ming 少 人); whether the few are Küchülüg’s men or both parties’ the words do not say.

sentences.t: Erdis-ün Buγdurma hužaγ̇ur-a qamtudču čerig(i)-jen žasažu ažuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: the Erdis (Irtysh), a river (Ming 水名) [水名的]
genitive: of (after a consonant, front-vowel form) [水名的]
Buqdurma, a place name (Ming 地名) [地名]
to be together, to join (from qamtu 'together'; stem inferred) [相合着]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form; the (i) is Shiratori's) [軍 自的行]
to prepare, set in order [整治着]

sentences.l: Erdis’ Buγdurma source-at together-joining, own army arranging, was.
sentences.i: and, drawn together at the source of the Buqdurma on the Erdis, they put their own troops in order.
sentences.n: hužaγ̇ur-a is hužaγ̇ur “root, source” (Ming 根源) in the dative-locative. Erdis-ün is the genitive of a river (Ming 水名的); Buγdurma is marked only 地名, “place name”, so I do not know whether it is a place at the Erdis’s head or a stream of the Erdis. qamtudču is qamtud- “join together” + -ču, žasažu žasa- “arrange, set in order”; čerig(i)-jen is “their own army”. ažuγ̇ui is a- “be” in the narrative past, so the chain ends “were arranging”. For the Erdis I give the printed name.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan kürčü bailduγ̇asu

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to face in battle order (stem inferred from the Ming 對陣) [對陣呵]

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan arriving, facing-battle if,
sentences.i: When Chinggis Qahan arrived and the lines faced one another,
sentences.n: kürčü is kür- “reach, arrive” with the converb -čü after r. bailduγ̇asu is baildu- “face in battle order” (stem inferred from the Ming 對陣) with -γ̇asu “if, when” (Ming 呵), as in oduγ̇asu above. The subject of baildu- is both sides; Toqto'a is picked out in the next unit.

sentences.t: Toγtoγ̇a tende šiba-jin sumun-a tusdažu unažuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: a stray shot (read from the Ming 亂箭 'random arrows'; uncertain) [亂箭 的]
genitive: of (after a vowel) [亂箭 的]
dative-locative: by (marks the agent of a passive) [箭行]
to strike, hit (stem inferred from the Ming 被射) [被射着]

sentences.l: Toγtoγ̇a there stray-arrow’s arrow-by being hit, had fallen.
sentences.i: Toqto'a was struck there by a stray arrow and fell.
sentences.n: tusdažu is tus- “strike, hit” (stem inferred from the Ming 被射) with the passive -da- and the converb -žu. sumun-a, “by the arrow”, is the dative-locative marking the agent of a passive (Ming 行). šiba-jin sumun is “an arrow of šiba”; the Ming 亂箭 gives “random arrows”, hence “stray”, but šiba itself I cannot find elsewhere. unažuγ̇u is una- “fall” in the narrative past. Whether he fell dead is told only by the next units.

sentences.t: Köġüd in-ü jasu in-ü barin jadažu

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to be unable (after a converb) [不能着]

sentences.l: Sons his bone his holding unable,
sentences.i: His sons could not take hold of his bones,
sentences.n: Köġüd in-ü is “his sons”: the third-person genitive in-ü stands after its noun, as in earlier parts. barin jadažu is a pattern to know: a converb followed by jada- “to be unable” (here -žu), so “unable to hold”. jasu is “bone” (Ming 骨頭); the Ming does not say whether the body or only the bones are meant, and the next unit speaks of the body, so I keep “bones” for jasu.

sentences.t: beje-ji in-ü abču odun jadažu

morph.gloss: accusative: object marker (the Ming 行) [身行]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to be unable (after a converb) [不能着]

sentences.l: Body-(object) his taking going unable,
sentences.i: could not carry off his body,
sentences.n: beje-ji in-ü is “his body (object)”; abču odun jadažu is “taking, going, unable”, two converbs (-ču, -un) making one act, “carry off”, then jada- “unable”, as in the unit above.

sentences.t: teriġü in-ü hoγtolžu abču jorčižuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to cut off (stem inferred from the Ming 斷) [割斷着]
to go off, set out (stem inferred from the Ming 去) [去了有]

sentences.l: Head his cutting off, taking, went.
sentences.i: and cut off his head, took it and went away.
sentences.n: teriġü in-ü is “his head”. hoγtolžu is hoγtol- “cut off” (stem inferred from the Ming 斷着). abču “taking” leads to the finite verb jorčižuγ̇u, jorči- “to go off” (stem inferred from the Ming 去了有) in the narrative past -žuγ̇u. That ends the chain whose subject is the sons.

sentences.t: Tende Naiman Merkid bolun qamtudču baildun jadažu

morph.gloss: to be together, to join [相合着]
to face in battle order [對陣]
to be unable (after a converb) [不能着]

sentences.l: There Naiman Merkid together, joining, facing-battle unable,
sentences.i: There the Naiman and the Merkid, together, joined forces but could not face the battle,
sentences.n: Naiman Merkid bolun is “Naiman, Merkid, being (together)”, bol- with -un (Ming 共 “together”). qamtudču “joining” as above. baildun jadažu is baildu- “face in battle order” + converb -n, then jada- “be unable”: the same pattern as barin jadažu.

sentences.t: buruγ̇uilan ködölürün

morph.gloss: to flee, evade (stem inferred from the Ming 逃) [逃]

sentences.l: fleeing, when moving,
sentences.i: fled, and as they moved off,
sentences.n: buruγ̇uilan is buruγ̇uila- “flee, evade” (stem inferred from the Ming 逃) with -n. ködölürün is ködöl- “move, set out” with the time-converb -ürün (Ming 動時). The chain goes on in the next unit.

sentences.t: Erdis-i ketülürün čübtüsčü oloṅki-jan usun-dur üküġülžüġüi.

morph.gloss: accusative: object marker (the Ming 行) [水名(行)]
to cross (a river; Ming 渡) [渡時]
to sink (stem inferred from the Ming 沉落) [沉落着]
most, the greater part (olon 'many' + -ki; analysis uncertain; Ming 多) [多 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own [多 自的行]
dative-locative: at, in, to (back-vowel form) [水裏]
narrative past (front-vowel form; Ming 來有) [敎 死了來有]

sentences.l: Erdis-(object) when crossing, sinking, most-their water-in were-made-to-die.
sentences.i: as they crossed the Erdis, most of them sank in the water and were drowned.
sentences.n: Erdis-i ketülürün is “the Erdis (object), when crossing”: ketül- is “cross a river” (Ming 渡) with -ürün. čübtüsčü is “sinking” (the stem čübtüs- inferred from the Ming 沉落着). oloṅki-jan is “most of them” (olon “many” plus an ending -ki; Ming 多 自的行; the build is uncertain) with the reflexive -jan. üküġülžüġüi is ükü- “die” + the causative -ġül- + the narrative past -žüġüi, literally “were made to die” (Ming 敎 死了來有); with no agent named I give “drowned”.

sentences.t: Čüġen γaruγsad Naiman Merkid Erdis-i ketülün baražu qaγačan ködölžüġüi.

morph.gloss: past participle plural: those who have …-ed [出了的每]
accusative: object marker (the Ming 行) [水名(行)]
to be finished, used up (here an auxiliary: 'completely') [了着]

sentences.l: The few who went out, Naiman Merkid, Erdis-(object) crossing finishing, parting, was moving.
sentences.i: The few who got out, Naiman and Merkid alike, crossed the Erdis and, parting from one another, moved on.
sentences.n: Čüġen γaruγsad is “the few who went out”: γar- + the plural participle -γsad. Naiman Merkid are set side by side, “Naiman, Merkid”. ketülün baražu, “crossing, finishing”, uses bara- “be finished” as an auxiliary meaning “having crossed completely” (Ming 了着). qaγačan is qaγača- “part, separate” + -n (Ming 分離). ködölžüġüi is ködöl- “move” in the narrative past, the front-vowel form of -žuγ̇ui.

sentences.t: Naiman-u Küčülüg Qān Uiγ̇urtai Qarluγ̇ud-i daγ̇arin

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (short form beside qaγan) [(皇帝)]
with, having (uncertain; the Ming gives only 種名) [種名]
the Qarluq, a people (Ming 種名) [種名行]
accusative: object marker (the Ming 行) [種名行]
to pass along, go by (Ming 經過) [經過]

sentences.l: Naiman’s Küčülüg Qān, Uighur-with(?), Qarluγ̇ud-(object) passing along,
sentences.i: Küchülüg Qan of the Naiman, going through the Uighurs and the Qarluqs,
sentences.n: daγ̇arin is daγ̇ari- “pass along, go by” (Ming 經過) with -n, which governs the accusative Qarluγ̇ud-i. The Qarluqs are the plural Qarluγ̇ud (Ming 種名).

sentences.i: He had those of them who were to be killed put to death, and the survivors he had his soldiers take captive.
sentences.n: Shiratori opens a mark before Kiduqun-i and never closes it; since talaγ̇ulba is a narrative past, I give the decree as reported narrative. an-u “their” follows its noun, like in-ü above (the back-vowel form). kiduqun-i is the uncertain word: the Ming 盡殺 means “kill utterly” and the stem is kidu-, but the ending -qun I cannot parse; I take it as “those to be killed”. kiduγ̇ulžu is the causative converb “having had killed”. hülegsed-i is the plural participle of hüle- “remain” (stem inferred from the Ming 餘剩) with the accusative. čeriġüd-te is “by (to) the soldiers”, the dative-locative -te marking the agent of a causative, as in talaγ̇ulba (tala- “plunder, take captive” + -γ̇ul-, past).

sentences.t: Basa urida oroγsan Merkid aγ̇uruγ̇ud-ača daičin bosčuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: to enter, come over (Ming 投入 'throw oneself into') [投入的]

sentences.i: Again, the Merkid who had earlier come over rose in revolt out of the rear camps.
sentences.n: oroγsan is oro- “enter” with the past participle -γsan; the Ming 投入 means “throw oneself into”, so I take it as “had come over, submitted”. aγ̇uruγ̇ud-ača is “from the rear camps” with the ablative -ača. daičin bosčuγ̇u is “hostility rose”: bos- “rise” in a narrative past; the Ming 反 gives the sense “revolt”. The Merkid had been taken into the camps and rose there.

sentences.n: The decree formula once more. What follows is in direct speech, and this time Shiratori’s marks open and close.

Tundaγa is “whole, entire” (Ming 全), ba “also, even” (Ming 也), which I leave to the literal line. aγ̇uluja is aγ̇ulu- “keep, preserve” (stem inferred from the Ming 敎存) with the hortative -ja “let us”; keġelüġe is keġe- “say” with a past in -lüġe (Ming 說來, “had said”). The speaker is Chinggis, quoting an earlier word of his own.

Who received them, and in what shares, is not said.

sentences.n: Shiratori opens a mark before Sübeġetei-ji, but see the note on the unit that begins Sübeġetej-e: the lines before the speech proper are narrated, so I put no marks on this one. temür teregetü-ji is “iron cart-having” (Ming 鐵 車子有的行): terege “cart”, the possessive -tü, the accusative -ji. It is an epithet; whether a nickname or a description of his baggage-cart I do not know. Both names take the accusative as the object of ilerün below.

sentences.n: köġüd-i in-ü is “his sons (object)”, the in-ü that follows its noun. nekeġülün is neke- “pursue” with the causative -ġül- and -n: “causing to pursue”. ilerün is ile- “send” with the time-converb -rün; the Ming gives 去時, “when going”, so “when he went” is possible, but then the object Sübeġetei-ji would be odd, and I keep “sending”.

sentences.t: Sübeġetej-e Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolžu:

morph.gloss: Sübegetei, a man's name [人名 行]
dative-locative: to (the j is a glide) [人名 行]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: Sübeġetei-to Čiṅgis Qaγan decree having-made:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan issued a decree to Sübegetei:
sentences.n: Sübeġetej-e is the dative-locative -e after a j glide (Ming 行). Here bolžu “having become/made” (Ming 做着) replaces bolurun, the same sense: “issuing a decree”. Shiratori has an opening mark before Sübeġetei-ji (two units above) and a second before Daγ̇u, the next unit, but only one closing mark follows, after gedkün far below. I take the speech proper to run from Daγ̇u to gedkün, and the lines above it as narrated. The other reading, that the first mark opens one speech running to gedkün, would have Chinggis name himself in the third person within his own words (“Chinggis Qaγan issued a decree”), so I do not take it; the doubled opening mark may be Shiratori’s slip.

sentences.t: "Daγ̇u bariγ̇ulurun

morph.gloss: voice, word, sound (Ming 把 'hold'; uncertain) [把]
to hold, take hold of [話時]

sentences.l: “Voice causing-to-hold when,
sentences.i: “When the word is given,
sentences.n: daγ̇u bariγ̇ulurun is uncertain. daγ̇u is “voice, sound, word”; bariγ̇ulurun is bari- “hold” with the causative -γ̇ul- and the time-converb -urun, “when making hold”, and the Ming 把話時 can mean “when holding the word”. I read it as “when the word (the order) is passed”, i.e. when the pursuit is begun; this is a guess from the Ming and the setting, and the whole speech after it holds. The same formula daγ̇u bariγ̇ulurun stands in §177 and §§178–181, where it is “charging with a message”; the reading here is of that kind.

These are all converbs describing what the sons do; the verb that closes the picture comes in the next unit.

sentences.t: qarbulčažu uγurγatu qulan sumutu buγu bolžu odba.

words.reading: 中合舌兒鏷(勒)察周 qarbulčažu

morph.gloss: to shoot (stem inferred from the Ming 射) [相射着]
reciprocal: at one another (Ming 相) [相射着]

words.reading: 兀中忽舌兒中合禿 uγurγatu

morph.gloss: arrow (the final n is lost before -tu) [帶箭 的]

sentences.l: mutually shooting, lasso-pole-having wild-ass, arrow-having deer becoming, went.
sentences.i: shoot at one another, become a wild ass with a lasso-pole and a deer with an arrow in it, and are gone.
sentences.n: This line is doubtful. qarbulčažu is qarbul- “shoot” (stem inferred from the Ming 射) with the reciprocal -ča- and -žu, “shooting at one another”. uγurγatu qulan is “lasso-pole-having wild ass” (uγurγa is the pole of the lasso, Ming 套竿; -tu “having”), sumutu buγu “arrow-having deer”: the Ming 帶套竿的 野馬, 帶箭 的 鹿. bolžu odba is “becoming, went”. I take it as the sons turned into hunted game and gone, set up as the first of the shapes that Sübegetei is told he must pursue in the units that follow; the sense of the whole sentence is uncertain. The Mongol verbs here are in the past (odba, “went”); I give them in the present, because they hang on the “When the word is given” of the unit above.

sentences.t: Teden-i žiġürtu bolžu nisčü teṅgeri-dür γaruγ̇asu

sentences.i: If they grow wings and fly up into the sky,
sentences.n: Teden-i, the accusative, stands first as the thing to be caught, which the verb in the next unit takes. žiġürtu is žiġür “wing” (Ming 翅) with -tu “having”. nisčü is nis- “fly” with -čü after s. teṅgeri-dür γaruγ̇asu is “if (they) go up into Heaven” (Ming 天行 上呵): γar- “go out, go up”, -uγ̇asu “if”. This opens a run of “if they become X, you become Y” conditions, each a rhetorical question.

sentences.t: čalir bolžu sokižu erižü ülü-ü güičekü či.

sentences.i: will you not become an iron spade, break the ground, search them out and overtake them?
sentences.n: čalir is “iron spade” (Ming 鐵鍬); I find the word nowhere else. sokižu is soki- “chisel, hack” (stem inferred from the Ming 鑿着), erižü eri- “seek”. güičekü is güiče- “overtake” (Ming 趕上) with the participle -kü; the question is carried by ülü-ü as above. sentences.i: If they become fish and go into the sea Tenggis,
sentences.n: žiγasun is “fish” (Ming 魚); Teṅgis a water name (Ming 水名), dalai-dur “in(to) the sea” (Ming 海 裏), with the dative-locative -dur; oroγ̇asu as above.

sentences.t: či Sübeġetei gölmi γubčiγ̇ur bolžu siġüžü qubčižu ülü-ü abqu či.

to scoop out, dip (Ming 撈) [撈着]
to levy, gather in (here the Ming reads 打 'strike, cast') [打着]
question particle (uncertain; the Ming puts its 麽 on the next word) [不]

sentences.l: you Sübeġetei circling-net drag-net becoming, scooping, netting, not-? take you.
sentences.i: will you, Sübegetei, not become a circling net and a drag net, scoop them up, net them and take them?
sentences.n: gölmi (Ming 旋網, “circling net”) and γubčiγ̇ur (拖網, “dragged net”) are found only here, so “circling net” and “drag net” are from the Ming alone. siġüžü is siġü- “scoop out” (Ming 撈); qubčižu is qubči-, elsewhere “levy, gather in”, here glossed 打 (“strike, cast”). abqu is ab- “take” with the participle -qu. The final či returns to the person addressed.

sentences.t: Basa ündür dabaγ̇a daban örgen müren ketülün ilebe.

morph.gloss: pass, ridge (Ming 嶺; from daba, cf. daba- “cross a pass”; the ending -γ̇a is a noun suffix of uncertain force) [嶺]

sentences.l: Again high pass crossing, wide river crossing, sent.
sentences.i: Again, over high passes and across wide rivers, I have sent you.
sentences.n: The sentence is hard. ilebe is ile- “send” in the past -be (Ming 敎去了), and the unit has no object. Since the speech is addressed to Sübegetei in the second person, I supply “you” and give it as a statement of what Chinggis has done; it may instead be the chronicler resuming, “he sent (him)”. dabaγ̇a is “pass” (read from the Ming 嶺 “ridge”), with the noun ending -γ̇a uncertain; daban and ketülün are the converbs of daba- “cross a pass” and ketül- “cross a river”.

sentences.t: Čima-ji γažar-un qola-ji sedkižü

morph.gloss: the oblique stem of či [你行]
accusative: object marker (the Ming 行) [你行]

accusative: object marker (the Ming 行) [遠行]

sentences.l: you-(object), land’s far-(object) thinking,
sentences.i: Thinking of you and of how far the land is,
sentences.n: Čima-ji is či “you” on the oblique stem čima- with the accusative (Ming 你行); qola-ji is qolo “far” with the accusative (Ming 遠行). sedkižü is sedki- “think” with -žü. I read both accusatives as objects of “thinking”: thinking of you, of the distance of the land. The speaker is considerate before the commands that follow.

sentences.t: čerig-ün ulaγ̇a turuγ̇ai üdüġüj-e qairaladqun

sentences.l: army’s horses lean before-not-yet, spare-you-all.
sentences.i: spare the army’s horses before they grow lean.
sentences.n: A construction to know: X-γ̇ai üdüġüj-e, “before X-ing” (üdüġüi “not yet”, Ming 未, with the dative-locative -e; the ending -γ̇ai I cannot parse). turuγ̇ai is the stem turu- “grow lean” (from turun “lean”, Ming 痩) with that ending. qairaladqun is qairala- “spare, cherish” (stem from the Ming 愛惜) with -dqun, the command to several (Ming 您): “you all, spare!”.

sentences.t: künesü-ben baraγ̇ai üdüġüj-e qučiγ̇adqun.

reflexive-possessive: one's own [行糧 自的行]
dative-locative (the j is a glide) [未行]
to be sparing, economize (Ming 省惜) [省惜您]

sentences.l: own-provisions finishing before-not-yet, economize-you-all.
sentences.i: Be sparing of your own food before it is used up.
sentences.n: The same pattern: baraγ̇ai üdüġüj-e “before it is finished” (bara- “be finished, used up”). künesü-ben is künesün “provisions” (the final n dropped before the ending) with the reflexive -ben “one’s own”. qučiγ̇adqun is qučiγ̇a- “economize” (Ming 省惜) with -dqun, the plural polite command.

sentences.t: Aγta turun baraγ̇asu qairalaγ̇asu ülü boluji.

morph.gloss: to grow lean (stem from turun 'lean', Ming 瘦) [瘦]
to be finished, used up (here an auxiliary: 'once done') [了了呵]

words.reading: 中合亦舌剌剌阿速 qairalaγ̇asu

sentences.l: Gelding lean having-become, finished if, sparing if, not will-serve.
sentences.i: Once the geldings have grown lean, sparing them will be of no use.
sentences.n: Aγta is “gelding” (Ming 騸馬). turun baraγ̇asu, “grown lean, once finished”, uses bara- as an auxiliary meaning “once it has come about”. qairalaγ̇asu is “if (you) spare”. ülü boluji is “not” + bol- “become” with an ending -uji I cannot parse; the Ming 中有 suggests “serve, be of use”, so “will not do”.

sentences.t: Künesün baran baraγ̇asu qučaγ̇asu ülü boluji.

morph.gloss: to be finished, used up (here an auxiliary: 'once done') [了呵]
to be sparing, economize (written qučaγ̇a- here) [省惜呵]
to become, to serve (Ming 中有) [中有]

sentences.l: Provisions finishing, finished if, economizing if, not will-serve.
sentences.i: Once the provisions are used up, economy will be of no use.
sentences.n: Parallel to the unit above: baran baraγ̇asu, “finished, once finished” (Ming 了 … 了呵), is “once wholly used up”. qučaγ̇asu is the same qučiγ̇a- written with a, plus -γ̇asu “if”.

sentences.t: Mör-tür tan-u göreġesün olon bi-že.

sentences.i: On the road you will find much game.
sentences.n: Mör-tür is “on the road” (mör “track”, Ming 路; dative-locative -tür). tan-u is “your” (ta, the plural polite pronoun, with the oblique n and the genitive; the same plural as -dqun). bi-že is bü- “be” (bi- before the particle -že “indeed”; Ming 有也者): “there is, indeed”. I supply no copula in the literal line beyond this verb.

to gallop, run a horse (Ming 去馬 / 走馬) [敎去馬您]

sentences.l: Beyond(?) thinking, going-about-at, army’s men-(object) game-at not let-gallop-you-all;
sentences.i: Thinking of what lies beyond, do not, while on the march, let the army’s men gallop after the game;
sentences.n: alus sedkižü is uncertain: alus stands in two earlier parts (“passing beyond” in §§140–143; “beyond” the mountain in §195), and the Ming here, 隔越, suggests “across, beyond”; sedkižü is “thinking”. “Thinking of what lies beyond” (or “ahead”) is only my guess at how the two fit. jabuqui-dur is jabu- “go about” with the participle -qui and the dative-locative: “at the going”, i.e. while on the march. qaγ̇ulγadqun is qaγ̇ul- “gallop (a horse)” (Ming 去馬 / 走馬) with the causative -γa- and -dqun; with bu “do not” it forbids sending men galloping at game (göreġesün-dür, Ming 野獸 行).

sentences.t: kem ügei bu abaladqun.

ending of the plural polite command: you (all) … [圍獵您]

sentences.i: do not hunt without limit.
sentences.n: kem ügei is “limit, without” (Ming 限 無). abaladqun is aba “hunt” (Ming 圍獵, the ring-hunt) with the verb-maker -la- and -dqun, “you all, hunt!”, here made a prohibition by bu.

sentences.t: čerig-ün küġün-e künesün-e nemeġesün öṅgekü-jen boltuγai keġen

morph.gloss: noun ending: an addition (Ming 添助) [添助]
cover(?) (Ming 𡓇葢; I cannot read the first character as a word; uncertain) [𡓇葢 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form) [𡓇葢 自的行]
optative, third person: let it be, let them … [敎做者︀]

sentences.l: Army’s men-to provisions-for addition, own cover let-be saying,
sentences.i: saying, ‘Let it be an addition to the food of the army’s men, a covering of their own,’
sentences.n: keġen “saying” closes a quotation inside the speech. nemeġesün is neme- “add” with a noun ending (Ming 添助, “help to add”). öṅgekü-jen is doubtful: the Ming 𡓇葢 has a first character I cannot read as a word, and 葢 means “cover”; with the reflexive -jen it is “their own …”. I give “covering”, but it is a guess at the sense; boltuγai is bol- “become” with the optative -tuγai, “let it be”.

sentences.t: abalabasu kemležü abaladqun.

conditional converb: if, when [圍獵 呵]

ending of the plural polite command: you (all) … [圍獵您]

sentences.l: hunting if, limiting, hunt-you-all.
sentences.i: when you do hunt, hunt within limits.
sentences.n: abalabasu is aba + the verb-maker -la- + -basu “if, when” (Ming 呵). kemležü is kemle- “to limit” (from kem “limit”; Ming 限着) with -žü. abaladqun is the plural polite command as above.

sentences.t: Kemten aba-dāča aṅgida čerig-ün küġün-ü emeġel-ün qudurγa bu qudurγalaγ̇ul.

morph.gloss: those having (plural possessive; Ming 有的每) [限有的(每)]
crupper, a strap under the tail (Ming 鞦) [鞦]

words.reading: 中忽都︀舌兒中合剌兀勒 qudurγalaγ̇ul

glyphs.s: 中忽都︀舌兒中合剌兀勒

sentences.l: Those-with-limits hunt-from apart, army’s man’s saddle’s crupper not make-put-on.
sentences.i: Apart from the limited hunt, do not have the cruppers put on the saddles of the army’s men.
sentences.n: Kemten aba-dāča aṅgida is read “apart from the hunt, the limited ones”: kem “limit” with -ten (Ming 限有的), aba “hunt” with the ablative -dāča (long vowel), aṅgida “apart, besides” (Ming 外); the exact link between kemten and the hunt is uncertain. emeġel-ün qudurγa is “the saddle’s crupper” (emeġel “saddle”, Ming 鞍子; qudurγa the strap under the horse’s tail, Ming 鞦). qudurγalaγ̇ul is qudurγa + -la- + the bare causative -γ̇ul as a command, “have a crupper put on”, with bu: “do not”.

sentences.t: Qadaγ̇ar ülü nemürgen sudalbižu jabutuγai.

morph.gloss: to hang on, fit (stem inferred from the Ming 搭) [敎搭]
to rein in, check the mouth (stem inferred from the Ming 閘口; uncertain) [不閘口着]
optative, third person: let it be, let them … [敎行者︀]

sentences.l: Bridle not causing-to-fit, mouth-not-checking, let-them-go.
sentences.i: Let them go with the bridle not fitted and the mouth not checked.
sentences.n: Qadaγ̇ar is “bridle” (Ming 轡頭). nemürgen is nemür- “hang on, fit” (stem inferred from the Ming 搭) with an ending -gen read from the Ming 敎 “cause”; ülü is “not”. sudalbižu is sudalbi- “check the mouth, rein in” (stem inferred from the Ming 閘口; uncertain) with -žu. jabutuγai is jabu- “go” with the optative -tuγai: “let them go”. The sense is that the horses are to be ridden easily; the details of the tack I do not trust.

sentences.t: Tein žasaldužu jabuγ̇asu čerig-ün küġün qaγ̇ulun ker čidaqu.

morph.gloss: to arrange, put in order [共整治着]
to gallop, run a horse (Ming 走馬) [走馬]
how, what manner (Ming 怎生) [怎生]

sentences.l: Thus arranging-together, going-if, army’s man horse-galloping how can.
sentences.i: If you march in order like this, how could an army man gallop his horse?
sentences.n: Tein žasaldužu is “thus arranging together”: žasa- “arrange” with the reciprocal -ldu- and -žu (Ming 共整治着). jabuγ̇asu is jabu- “go” with -γ̇asu “if”. qaγ̇ulun is qaγ̇ul- “gallop (a horse)” with -n (Ming 走馬). ker čidaqu is “how can (he)?” (Ming 怎生 能), a rhetorical question that means “he cannot”.

sentences.t: Ein žasaγlažu böġed žasaγ dabaγsad-i barižu nišitügei.

morph.gloss: makes a verb: to make a rule [法度着]
converb ending (uncertain): then, thereupon (Ming 便) [便]
law, regulation, military discipline (Ming 軍法) [軍法]
to transgress, go beyond (Ming 越) [越了的每 行]
past participle plural: those who have …-ed [越了的每 行]
accusative: object marker (the Ming 行) [越了的每 行]

sentences.l: Thus rule-making, then army-law transgressing-ones-(object) seizing, let-strike.
sentences.i: Once the rule is made, whoever breaks the army’s law is to be seized and beaten.
sentences.n: Ein žasaγlažu is “thus making a rule”: žasaγ “law” with -la- and -žu (Ming 法度着). böġed is bü- “be” with an ending -ġed (uncertain), read as “then, thereupon” (Ming 便). dabaγsad-i is daba- “go beyond, transgress” with the plural participle -γsad and the accusative: “those who transgressed”. barižu nišitügei is “seizing, let (them) strike”; nišitügei is niši- “strike” (stem uncertain, from the Ming 打) with the third-person optative -tügei (Ming 者). The one who beats is not named, and I give it as a passive. The speech goes on in the next unit.

sentences.t: Bidan-u žarliγ dabaγsad-i bidan-a taniγdaqun metüs-i bidan-a ögčü iredkün.

genitive of the pronoun: our [俺的]
to transgress, go beyond (Ming 越) [越了的每 行]

accusative: object marker (the Ming 行) [越了的每 行]
we (inclusive; the Ming here 俺) [俺行]

to know, recognize (Ming 認) [認的每]

we (inclusive; the Ming here 俺) [俺行]

ending of the plural polite command: you (all) … [敎來您]

sentences.l: Our decree transgressing-ones-(object), to-us known such-(object), to-us giving, come-you-all.
sentences.i: Those who break our decree, such of them as are known to us, hand over to us.
sentences.n: bidan-u “our” and bidan-a “to us” are the inclusive we (bida, the oblique stem bidan-); the Ming writes 俺 here, where earlier it often has 咱, the alternation noted in other parts. dabaγsad-i is “those who transgressed”, as in the unit above. taniγdaqun is tani- “know, recognize” (Ming 認的每) with a plural participle ending I cannot divide; metüs-i is “the likes, such” (metü “like”, plural -s, accusative). bidan-a taniγdaqun is “known to us”, the dative-locative naming the one who knows. ögčü iredkün is “giving, come”, the Ming 與着 敎來您, here “hand over”; -dkün is the plural polite command.

sentences.t: bidan-a ülü taniγdaqun olon-i mün tende böġed mököriġülüdkün.

ending of the plural polite command: you (all) … [處斬您]

sentences.l: To-us not known many-(object), just there then, have-executed-you-all.
sentences.i: The many who are not known to us, have them cut down on the spot.
sentences.n: Parallel to the unit above: ülü taniγdaqun “not known”, olon-i “the many” (Ming 多行). mün tende, “just there” (Ming 只 那裏), makes “on the spot”; böġed is “then” (Ming 便). mököriġülüdkün is mököri- “cut down, behead” (Ming 處斬您, “have them beheaded”; the stem as in mököriġüldekün, §§149–150) with the causative -ġül- and -dkün, the plural polite command.

sentences.t: Müren-ü činaγ̇un mösekdükün ta.

morph.gloss: that side, the far side (Ming 那廂行; uncertain analysis) [那廂行]
part, separate (Ming 分離; stem and ending uncertain) [分離]

sentences.l: River’s that-side-to, part-you-all, you.
sentences.i: On the far side of the river, you are to part from one another.
sentences.n: This line and the two that follow are doubtful. Müren-ü is “of the river” (front-vowel genitive); činaγ̇un is “to that side” (Ming 那廂行), the far side; mösekdükün is “part, separate” from the Ming 分離, with a stem and ending I cannot divide; ta is “you” (plural, polite). I read an instruction for how the force is to move on the far side of a river and of a mountain, but the reason is not given.

sentences.t: Mün josu-γ̇ar jabudqun.

custom, proper way, rule (Ming 道理) [道理 依着]

ending of the plural polite command: you (all) … [行每您]

sentences.l: Just custom-by go-you-all.
sentences.i: Go only by the rule.

that side, the far side (Ming 那廂行; uncertain analysis) [那廂行]

morph.gloss: to part, scatter (Ming 分離; stem uncertain) [分離]
ending of the plural polite command: you (all) … [分離]

sentences.l: Mountain’s that-side-to, scatter-you-all, you.
sentences.i: On the far side of the mountain, scatter.
sentences.n: Aγ̇ula-jin činaγ̇un is “to the far side of the mountain” (Ming 山 的 那廂行), the pair of müren-ü činaγ̇un above. alγasaldudqun is glossed 分離 like mösekdükün, with the reciprocal -ldu- and the plural polite command -dqun; the stem alγasa- is uncertain.

sentences.t: Aṅgida öġere bu sedkidkün.

morph.gloss: ending of the plural polite command: you (all) … [想您]

sentences.l: Besides otherwise not think-you-all.
sentences.i: Think of nothing else besides.
sentences.n: aṅgida öġere is “besides, otherwise” (Ming 外 別), a doubled adverb; bu is the prohibitive “do not”, sedkidkün sedki- “think” with the plural polite command.

sentences.t: Müṅke teṅgeri-de küčü aγ̇uγa nemegdežü

morph.gloss: Heaven, the sky as a power [天 行]
dative-locative: by (front-vowel form; names the doer of a passive) [天 行]
strength, vigour (Ming 氣力; the word is not found elsewhere) [氣力]

sentences.l: Eternal Heaven-by strength strength being-added,
sentences.i: With strength and might added by Eternal Heaven,
sentences.n: Müṅke teṅgeri, “Eternal Heaven” (müṅke Ming 長生). teṅgeri-de is the dative-locative -de naming the doer of a passive, “by Heaven” (Ming 行), here before nemegdežü, neme- “add” with the passive -gde- and -žü. küčü aγ̇uγa are two words for “strength” (Ming 氣力 氣力), a pair; aγ̇uγa I find nowhere else.

sentences.t: Toγtoγ̇a-jin köġüd-i γar-tur(i)-jan oroγ̇uluγ̇asu bidan-dur abčiratala jaγ̇un bi.

morph.gloss: Toqto'a, a man's name [人名 的]
genitive: of (after a vowel) [人名 的]
accusative: object marker (the Ming 行) [子每行]

words.reading: 中合舌兒-都︀舌里-顏 γar-tur(i)-jan

morph.gloss: dative-locative: in (the (i) is Shiratori's) [手 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own [手 自的行]
conditional: if, when (u a linking vowel) [被入呵]
we (inclusive; the Ming here 咱) [咱行]
dative-locative of the pronoun: to us [咱行]
to bring along (ab- “take” plus a second verb; form uncertain; Ming 將來) [將來直到]
until, as far as [將來直到]
is, exists (a short form of bü-) [有]

sentences.l: Toγtoγ̇a’s sons-(object) own-hand-in entering-caused if, to-us until-bringing, what is.
sentences.i: if the sons of Toqto'a are put into your own hands, what need is there to bring them as far as us?
sentences.n: oroγ̇uluγ̇asu is oro- “enter” with the causative -γ̇ul- and -γ̇asu “if”: “if they are made to enter” (Ming 被入呵). γar-tur(i)-jan is “in (their) own hand”, with the reflexive pointing back to ta, “you”, so “into your hands”. abčiratala is abčira- “bring along” (ab- “take” plus a second verb, as in abčiražü; Ming 將來) with -tala “until, as far as”. jaγ̇un bi is “what is?” (Ming 甚麽 有). I read it as a rhetorical question, “what need is there?”; this is a reading from the Ming, not certain.

sentences.t: Tende ta gedkün"

morph.gloss: there, then (locative adverb from tere 'that') [那裏]
to cast aside, throw away (Ming 棄了; reading uncertain) [棄了]
ending of the plural polite command: you (all) … [棄了]

sentences.l: There you cast-aside-you-all.”
sentences.i: Cast them aside there.”
sentences.n: ge- is “cast aside, throw away” (Ming 棄了; some earlier parts read the same word as gedkü-; the reading is uncertain), -dkün the plural polite command. “Cast aside” may here mean “put out of the way”, that is, kill them; the Ming does not say. The single closing mark Shiratori prints, after gedkün, ends the speech that began at Daγ̇u.

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Saying, decree made.
sentences.i: So he spoke, and issued the decree.
sentences.n: keġen “saying” and bolba “made” (Ming 做了) with žarliγ close the decree reported from the start of §199: the whole is the report of what Chinggis decreed, and the words from Daγ̇u to gedkün are his speech within it.

sentences.t: Sübeġetei-je basa Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:

morph.gloss: dative-locative: to (the j is a glide) [人名行]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: Sübeġetei-to again Čiṅgis Qaγan when saying:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Sübegetei:
sentences.n: Sübeġetei-je is the dative-locative after a j glide (Ming 人名行). ügülerün is ügüle- “speak, say” with the time-converb -rün (Ming 說), here “when speaking”, which I give as the past. A second speech begins in the next unit, with its opening mark.

sentences.t: "Čima-ji ajalaγ̇ulurun bi

morph.gloss: the oblique stem of či [你行]
accusative: object marker (the Ming 行) [你行]
to go out on campaign, march out (stem inferred from the Ming 出征) [敎出征時]
converb of time: when …-ing [敎出征時]

sentences.l: “You-(object) sending-on-campaign when, I —
sentences.i: “As I send you out on campaign —
sentences.n: Čima-ji is the accusative of “you” (Ming 你行). ajalaγ̇ulurun is ajala- “go on campaign” (stem inferred from the Ming 出征) with the causative -γ̇ul- and the time-converb -urun: “when sending out on campaign” (Ming 敎出征時). bi is “I”. The sentence is broken off by a dash because its thought is completed in the unit that follows.

sentences.t: üčügen čaγ-tur γurban Merkid-ün Uduid-ta Burqan-Qaldun-(n)i γurbanta qučiγ̇ulžu ajuγ̇uldalaγ̇a bi.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at, in, to (back-vowel form) [時裏]
the Merkid, a people [種名 的]
genitive: of (after a consonant) [種名 的]
the Uduid, a clan of the Merkid (Ming 姓 'surname') [姓(名)(行)]
dative-locative: by (marks the agent of a passive) [姓(名)(行)]

words.reading: 不舌峏中罕-中合勒敦-泥 Burqan-Qaldun-(n)i

glyphs.s: 不舌峏中罕-中合勒敦-泥

morph.gloss: Burqan Qaldun, the holy mountain of the Mongols (Ming 山名) [山名行]
to circle, go round (stem inferred from the Ming 繞着) [敎繞着]
to fear, be afraid (from the Ming 怕) [被敎怕來]

sentences.l: Small time-at, three Merkid’s Uduid-by Burqan-Qaldun-(object) three-times circling-having-caused, was-made-afraid, I.
sentences.i: when I was small, the Uduid of the three Merkid made me go three times round Burqan Qaldun, and I was afraid.
sentences.n: üčügen čaγ-tur is “at the small time”, in childhood. γurban Merkid-ün Uduid-ta is “by the Uduid of the three Merkid”: -ta is the dative-locative marking the doer of a passive (Ming 行), here of ajuγ̇uldalaγ̇a, aju- “fear” with the causative -γ̇ul- (“frighten”), the passive -da- and the narrative past -laγ̇a (Ming 被敎怕來, “was made afraid”). Burqan-Qaldun-(n)i is the accusative, the thing gone round; qučiγ̇ulžu is qučiγ- “go round” with the causative: “making (me) circle”, the “me” being understood. γurbanta is “three times” (Ming 三次).

sentences.t: Teimü öšiten irgen-i edöġe basa aman kelen aldažu odčuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: so, thus, it is so (adverb) [那般有]
grudge, feud (read from the Ming 讐) [讐有的(每)]
people, the common folk [百姓 行]
accusative: object marker (the Ming 行) [百姓 行]
to let go, to swear (the Ming here 放着 'let go'; elsewhere 誓 'swear') [放着]

sentences.l: So feud-having people-(object) now again mouth word letting-go went.
sentences.i: So now, once more, I have let my word go and set out against the feuding people.
sentences.n: This line is uncertain. öšiten irgen-i is “the feud-having people (object)” (öši “feud” from the Ming 讐; -ten “those having”). aman kelen is “mouth, word”, and aldažu is aldaž-, which the Ming here glosses 放着 “letting go” (it was 誓 “swear” in earlier parts): so “giving one’s word”, “declaring”. odčuγ̇ui is od- “go” in the past; the subject is not given, and I take it to be the speaker (the Khan). The object is öšiten irgen-i, and the sense “against” is mine.

sentences.t: urtu-jin üžüġür-e gün-(n)ü hiruγ̇ar-a kürülčetügei keġen nekeġülün üžüġüren

morph.gloss: genitive: of (after a vowel) [長 的]
end, tip (Ming 稍頭) [稍頭 行]
dative-locative: at, to (front-vowel form) [稍頭 行]
to come together (kür- “reach” + -ül- + -če-, as in kürülčežü; here Ming 敎共到) [敎共到者︀]
optative, third person: let … (Ming 者) [敎共到者︀]
until, right to (Ming 直到; uncertain) [直到頭]

sentences.l: Long’s tip-to, deep’s bottom-to, let-be-made-to-reach-together, saying, pursuit-causing right-to-the-end,
sentences.i: Saying, ‘Let it reach the end of the long and the bottom of the deep,’ I had them pursued to the very end;
sentences.n: urtu-jin üžüġür-e gün-(n)ü hiruγ̇ar-a is “to the end of the long, to the bottom of the deep” (Ming 長 的 稍頭行, 深的 底行), a phrase for “however far”. kürülčetügei is kürülče- “come together” (kür- “reach” with -ül- and -če-, as in kürülčežü in earlier parts) and the optative -tügei (Ming 敎共到者, “let them be brought to arrive together”); the subject is unstated, so “it” is mine. keġen “saying”. nekeġülün is the causative “making pursue”; üžüġüren is üžüġür “end” with -en (Ming 直到頭, “right to the end”).

sentences.t: temür terege deledčü hüker žil čaγ̇uraγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: to strike, hammer, forge (Ming 打造) [打造着]
to go out on campaign (stem inferred from the Ming 出征) [敎出征了]

sentences.l: Iron cart having-forged, ox year caused-to-march.
sentences.i: I forged an iron cart, and in the Ox year sent you on campaign.
sentences.n: temür terege is “iron cart” (Ming 鐵 車), the cart behind the epithet temür teregetü of Sübegetei above. deledčü is dele- “strike, forge” (Ming 打造着) with the converb -dčü. čaγ̇uraγ̇ulba is čaγ̇ura- (stem inferred from the Ming 出征) with the causative -γ̇ul- and the past -ba: “caused to go on campaign”. No subject or object is stated; “I” and “you” are supplied from the sense. hüker žil is the same Ox year as in §198.

sentences.t: Bidan-i ečine ber böġesü ile metü

morph.gloss: we (inclusive; the Ming here 咱) [咱行]
accusative of the pronoun: us [咱行]
behind, at the back (Ming 背處) [背處]
conditional: if (written böġesü; Ming 有呵) [有呵]
openly, face to face (Ming 對面) [對面]

sentences.l: Us-(object) behind even if-be, face-to-face like,
sentences.i: Even if you are behind us, it is as if face to face;
sentences.n: Bidan-i is the accusative of the inclusive we; ečine “behind, at the back” (Ming 背處). ber böġesü is “even if it is” (ber “even”, böġesü “if it be”, Ming 也 有呵), a pattern that repeats in the next unit. ile metü is “like face to face” (ile Ming 對面; metü “like”). The grammatical subject is not given; “you” is understood.

sentences.t: qolo ber böġesü oira metü

morph.gloss: conditional: if (written böġesü; Ming 有呵) [有呵]

sentences.l: Far even if-be, near like,
sentences.i: and if far, as if near;
sentences.n: The same pattern as the unit above: qolo ber böġesü, “even if it is far” (qolo, Ming 遠), oira metü, “like near” (Ming 近 般).

sentences.t: sedkižü jabuγ̇asu deġere teṅgeri-de ber igeġegdemüi-že ta"

morph.gloss: Heaven, the sky as a power [天 行]
dative-locative: by (front-vowel form; names the doer of a passive) [天 行]
to protect, help (stem inferred from the Ming 護助) [被護助有也者︀]
present tense: is [被護助有也者︀]
assertion particle: indeed, surely [被護助有也者︀]

sentences.l: thinking, if going, above Heaven-by also is-protected-indeed you.”
sentences.i: think so as you go, and you will be protected by Heaven above as well.”
sentences.n: sedkižü “thinking”, jabuγ̇asu “if going” (Ming 想着 行呵). deġere teṅgeri-de ber is “also by Heaven above” (Ming 上 天行 也): -de marks the doer of a passive, as with müṅke teṅgeri-de above. igeġegdemüi-že is igeġe- “protect, help” (stem inferred from the Ming 護助) with the passive -gde-, the present -müi and the assertion particle -že (Ming 被護助有也者). ta is “you” (plural, polite); the closing mark is Shiratori’s.

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Saying, decree made.
sentences.i: So he spoke, and issued the decree.
sentences.n: keġen žarliγ bolba as above, closing the second speech and the part.
